annotations.text:
The problem

The species and the place are both drawn as prose under the name, so the eye has to read the words to tell which is which. Making the place smaller and fainter says 'less important' — but they are not two points on one scale. The species is what the plant IS; the place is where it happens to be standing. Different kinds of fact.

Four ways to say that, on both lists at once.

NOW

Same prose, 12px/ink-faint under 13px/ink-muted. It works, but only once you have read both lines. On the row the place also truncates mid-word when the right-hand figure is wide.

Here as the thing to beat.

LABEL REGISTER  ·  recommended

The place is set in the app's own place type: 12px, uppercase, tracked — the same specimen the drawer label uses to say SLAAPKAMER above a group. So a place looks like a place wherever it appears, and the change of register does the separating: no dot, no fading contest.

The app already argues for this. Section's own source note: a heading 'has to be a different KIND of type from the labels under it, not a heavier weight of the same one'.

Tradeoff: caps run long, so a room like Studeerkamer eats more width than it does in sentence case.

ITS OWN LANE

The place leaves the text entirely. On the tile it becomes a chip on the picture — the same floating pill the archive tag already uses; on the row it takes a fixed 84px lane before the figure.

Strongest structural win: the tile is the SAME HEIGHT in both sorts, so the grid stops going ragged when you switch to A–Z, and nothing can truncate the species.

Tradeoff: a chip on a photograph is busier than a chip on paper, and the lane costs the name 84px on every row for a fact you only sometimes want.

WITH ITS PIN

The place keeps its prose and gains the pin — the same glyph the form already puts over 'Where it lives'. The glyph classifies it instantly; you never have to work out which line is which.

Tradeoff: one pin per row and per tile at list scale is a lot of small marks on a page whose whole manner is quiet, and an 11px pin is close to mush.

LET THE GROUPING CARRY IT

Don't show it. Sorted A–Z the place is simply absent; 'By place' is one tap away and then the drawer label says it, in full, once per group instead of once per row.

The cheapest answer and the cleanest picture: constant tile height, nothing to rank, nothing to truncate.

Tradeoff: you cannot see name and room at once in A–Z. If 'which Calathea is the bedroom one' is a real question at the shelf, this fails it — and that is the question worth answering before picking.

Worth saying: the two nearest neighbours mix well. The label register on the row (where width is cheap) and the lane/chip on the tile (where a constant height is worth most) is a defensible pair — the rule stays 'a place is never prose', and each list gets the form that suits its shape.
